subject: Staged buffer strategy — OEM lead times + cloud fallback confirmation
body:
From: Rajiv Sharma <rs@orion-oem.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preliminary OEM quote + realistic lead times for Q3 onramp

Ben —

Attached is the preliminary quote for the 8x A800 nodes you flagged (Orion_OEM_quote_20270501.pdf). Two quick notes: 1) current queue for A800 production is ~14–18 weeks from PO; 2) we can prioritize a small lot (up to 20 units) for a 10–12 week turnaround if you accept a 7% expedite premium.

We can also split shipping — initial weeks 10–12 for a small buffered delivery, remainder shipped on standard cadence. If you need an immediate bridge, we can coordinate an NRE for a short-term rental program via our logistics partner.

Let me know target dates and whether you want us to hold inventory for you.

—Rajiv
Orion OEM (sales)
rs@orion-oem.com

Attachments: Orion_OEM_quote_20270501.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>; Cc: Rajiv Sharma <rs@orion-oem.com>, Eva Morales <eva@cloudscale.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary OEM quote + realistic lead times for Q3 onramp

Team —

Forwarding Rajiv's quote. High-level ask: Acme wants dedicated capacity to start onboarding customers in early Sep (week of Sep 6). The deal triggers are set for mid-July if procurement signs. We need a pragmatic plan that ties our Dedicated sizing + order cadence to both OEM deliveries and cloud fallback for excess shortfall.

Questions for internal owners (please reply inline):
- Marissa: allocation priority — how many RUs should we reserve for the Acme deal in the Sep window vs general backlog?
- Dev: rough VM/GPU node sizing and staging plan for a staggered rollout (can we start with a pilot pool of ~40 GPUs and ramp to 240 across two months?)
- Karthik: will finance accept a staged payment/holdback to secure an expedite batch?

Proposed decision (initial): 1) Procure an expedited buffer of 20 A800s (12-week ETA) to cover pilot + early scaling; 2) Book additional standard-order batch (180 units) on 16–18 week lead time for full capacity; 3) Contract cloud fallback (Cloudscale) for up to 60 GPUs reserved as transient capacity if OEM shipments slip past Sep 20.

Rajiv/Eva — please confirm that options above are feasible. Rajiv: can Orion hold 20 units on expedite with a PO? Eva: can Cloudscale commit a 60-GPU reserved pool with cancellation flexibility (14-day notice) and a per-hour charge cap?

Thanks —
Ben
Sr. Account Exec, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx (planning sheet)

---

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary OEM quote + realistic lead times for Q3 onramp

Ben / team —

Quick sizing notes from infra:
- Pilot (Phase 0): 20 A800s -> provides ~160 vGPU slots at conservative limits; good for sandbox + initial ingestion.
- Phase 1 (early Sep ramp): ~40 additional A800s (total 60) to validate throughput and latency SLOs for Acme's anticipated baseline traffic.
- Phase 2 (full onramp): remaining 180 units to reach target 240 A800s by end of Oct; we stagger shipments across two 8-week windows to avoid capacity shock.

Operational considerations:
- Staggered bringing-up is required: PV pool for canary models, then steady-state. Dedicated network and KMS provisioning can be done in parallel: estimate 3 weeks once first hardware arrives.
- KV cache warmup means we need pilot traffic to be routed to the pilot pool; plan for a 48–72 hour warm window after provisioning.

Impact on costs: accelerate 20-unit expedite increases hardware line item ~7% + expedite logistics (~$18k). Cloud fallback cost estimate (if used 60 GPUs for 4 weeks): ~$120k gross, but should be largely consumed only if OEM slips >2 weeks.

I've attached the sizing workbook (dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx). If we accept Rajiv's expedite, we should issue PO for the 20-unit buffer to Orion and include a 30% deposit; finance to confirm.

—Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rs@orion-oem.com>, Eva Morales <eva@cloudscale.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmeai.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Preliminary OEM quote + realistic lead times for Q3 onramp

Thanks all — plan below is what we'll execute unless anyone flags a hard blocker by EOD Friday (May 7):

1) Ben -> Orion (Rajiv): PO for 20 expedited A800s with 30% deposit. Please confirm a firm ETA window (earliest/ latest) and whether units can be held on our ASN for up to 30 days post-production. We will sign expedite addendum. (Attachment: Orion_OEM_quote_20270501.pdf)

2) Ben -> Cloudscale (Eva): Please confirm a short-term reserved pool: 60 GPUs start Sep 1 through Sep 30 with cancellation window 14 days prior and hourly cost cap not to exceed quoted estimate. If we trigger fallback, Redwood will pay hourly + an activation fee. Please send standard MSA addendum or PO text so we can route to procurement. (Requested attachment: cloudscale_fallback_commit.pdf)

3) Marissa/Finance (Karthik): Approve the 30% deposit for the 20-unit expedite and confirm how that will map to the ACME billing milestone (we will push as cost-of-goods for the deal). Need approval by May 7 EOD.

4) Dev/Infra: prepare the staging runbook and reserve a 48–72 hour window for warmup after first inventory arrives. Link the runbook into HubSpot deal (I added the doc).

Acme procurement — tagging you to confirm the deal timing is still unchanged (mid-July signature target). If your schedule slips earlier or later, tell us so we can adjust the expedite and fallback sizing.

I'll execute the PO once Rajiv confirms ETA and once Karthik greenlights the deposit.

Cheers —
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Exec, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Orion_OEM_quote_20270501.pdf, cloudscale_fallback_commit.pdf
